node.title: Re: Minimally changing combinations (updated!)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I think you're looking for [wp://Heap's algorithm], although a quick search on CPAN and a look on [https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Permutations#Perl|Rosettacode] doesn't yet show me an existing Perl implementation. Update: Sorry, that was permutations, you're looking for combinations.

Update 2019-10-05: I've just released this as [mod://Algorithm::Odometer::Gray]!

Update 2: Knuth's "The Art of Computer Programming", "Generating all n-tuples", Algorithm H, "Loopless reflected mixed-radix Gray generation". Best I can do at the moment is an implementation in Python from the Sage project, [https://github.com/sagemath/sage/blob/master/src/sage/combinat/gray_codes.py#L19|here]. Update 3: The exact same algorithm appears to be described in this freely available paper: [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221440132_Loopless_Functional_Algorithms|Loopless Functional Algorithms] as "Algorithm C" in the section "9.5. Non-binary Gray codes".

Final Update: I think I've implemented the algorithm as described:

sub mixedgray_it { my @w = @_; my @m = map { 0+@$_ } @w; die "all items must have at least two positions" if grep {$_<2} @m; my @a = (0) x @m; my @f = 0 .. @m; my @o = (1) x @m; my $done; return sub { return undef if $done; my $rv = [map {$w[$_][$a[$_]]} 0..$#w]; if ($f[0]==@w) { $done=1; return $rv } my $j = $f[0]; $f[0] = 0; $a[$j] += $o[$j]; if ($a[$j]==0 || $a[$j]==$m[$j]-1) { $o[$j] = -$o[$j]; $f[$j] = $f[$j+1]; $f[$j+1] = $j+1; } return $rv; } } use Data::Dump; my $it = mixedgray_it(['a','b','c'],[1,2]); while (defined( my $c = $it->() )) { dd $c } __END__ ["a", 1] ["b", 1] ["c", 1] ["c", 2] ["b", 2] ["a", 2]
